text: The pilot's skill is by no means equally proved in a calm as in a storm: in the former case he tamely enters the port, unnoticed and unapplauded; but when the cordage cracks, the mast bends, and the rudder groans, then it is that he shines out in all his glory.
author: Pliny the Younger
translation: William Melmoth, rev. F. C. T. Bosanquet
